subject: Orion-13B: 503/timeout spike — customer update and RCA draft
messages:

Subject: Sudden 503s from Orion-13B since 08:45 PT

Hi Lauren,

We started seeing ~15% 503s and a number of timeouts across our production fleet using the Orion-13B model at ~08:45 PT. Errors are concentrated on requests with prompt lengths > 1,000 tokens but some short prompts are affected too. Our customers are reporting degraded chat experiences. We attached a short screencap of the console where errors spike.

Can Redwood confirm whether this is an infrastructure, model, or routing issue? We need an ETA on mitigation — our SREs are on standby.

Thanks,
Tom

From: dev.patel@redwood.ai

Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-25T09:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden 503s from Orion-13B since 08:45 PT

Folks — quick tech note, interim findings:
- Evidence suggests a scheduling regression in the serving runtime when sequence length > 1k. We see increased KV cache eviction and a handful of kernels hitting a retry path that returns 503.
- No recent model parameter change in the last 48h; however, an automated kernel selector patch rolled out to canary yesterday and partially to us-west.
- I kicked a rollback of the kernel-selector patch for the affected pool at 09:33 PT; initial telemetry shows dropped 503 rate from 15% -> ~4% in the first 10 minutes.

Immediate actions taken:
- Rollback of the kernel-selector patch in affected pool (us-west-2)
- Activated fallback routing to quantized Orion-13B (orion-13b-q4) for requests with sequence length > 1k
- Collected logs and stack traces (attachment: orion-503-logs.tar.gz) and pushed to the shared drive (link in metadata).

Next steps:
- Continued monitoring for 2 hours, then assess whether a full-service rollback is required.
- Prepare RCA draft for review — suspect root cause: incorrect kernel selection heuristic under rare sequence-length distribution.

— Dev Patel
Senior SRE | Redwood Inference
Attachment: orion-503-logs.tar.gz (log archive, 12MB)

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

Date: 2027-04-25T10:10:00Z
Subject: Customer update — Orion-13B 503s (interim mitigation in place)

Tom / Sarah — quick update on the incident:

What happened (high level):
- Starting ~08:45 PT we saw a spike in 503s affecting some requests to Orion-13B. Root cause appears related to a kernel selection heuristic interacting poorly with long-context requests.

What we did:
- Rolled back the recent kernel-selector patch in the affected pool (us-west-2).
- Activated fallback routing to orion-13b-q4 for long prompts to avoid the problematic kernel path.
- Collected logs and traces; we’ve uploaded them to the shared drive and attached a log bundle for your SREs.

Impact:
- Measured 503 rate reduced from ~15% to <3% post-mitigation. Short prompt traffic largely stable.

ETA / next steps:
- Monitoring window: 4 hours.
- By EOD PT we’ll provide an RCA draft and a recommended plan to prevent recurrence (we suspect a selector heuristic regression).
- If you see any residual 503s or regressions, please reply with a few request IDs (or the logs) and we’ll prioritize those.

We realize this interrupted your customers and appreciate your patience. Marissa will coordinate any billing/credits conversations if needed; we’ll also propose an engineering preventive action in the RCA.

Best,
Lauren
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@orbitai.com>, Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@orbitai.com>, OrbitAI Support <support@orbitai.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-29T17:45:00Z
Subject: RCA draft — Orion-13B 503/TIMEOUT spike (Apr 25) + planned remediation

Tom / Sarah — attaching the RCA draft for the Apr 25 incident and the remediation timeline. Summary below; full RCA is attached (rca-draft-20270429.pdf).

Summary:
- Root cause: a kernel-selector heuristic update (canary -> partial rollout) caused incompatible kernel choices when sequence length > 1k, causing excessive retries and transient 503s in specific serving pools.
- Immediate mitigation: rollback of kernel-selector patch and routing to orion-13b-q4 for affected requests; reduced 503 rate to <2%.
- Contributing factor: insufficient canary traffic coverage for long-sequence workloads during rollout.

Planned remediation:
- Improve canary selection to include long-sequence traffic mirrors (INF-1452).
- Add a runtime guard to prevent selector from choosing experimental kernels for requests > 1k tokens. (2-week sprint)
- Expand telemetry alerts to detect kernel-level error spikes earlier.

Customer-facing remediation & compensation:
- We’ll offer a modest usage credit for time window 08:45–10:30 PT. Marissa will follow up to confirm amounts and process.

Requested next steps from OrbitAI:
- Please confirm if OrbitAI needs additional log extracts or more granular request IDs.
- Let us know a good time for a short postmortem call (20–30m) next week to walk through the RCA draft and timeline.

Attachments: rca-draft-20270429.pdf (RCA draft, 6 pages), orion-503-logs.tar.gz (collected traces)

Thanks again for your patience. We’ll finalize the RCA after feedback and schedule a call.

— Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
